question: The location of ‘Dhamek Stupa’ is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarnath**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhamek Stupa** is located in **Sarnath**.
 
• Sarnath is a famous pilgrimage site for Buddhists and is located near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• The stupa was built by the Mauryan emperor **Ashoka** in 249 BCE.
 
• It marks the spot where Buddha is said to have given his first sermon to his five disciples after attaining enlightenment, known as the **Dharmachakra Pravartana (Turning of the Wheel of Dharma)**.
 
• The Dhamek Stupa is one of the most visited and revered Buddhist structures in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The original stupa, commissioned by Ashoka, was a simple structure, but it was later expanded and embellished during the Gupta period.
 
• Sarnath also houses the remains of several other ancient structures, including monasteries and temples, which reflect the rich cultural and religious heritage of the site.
 
• Excavations at Sarnath have uncovered a wealth of artifacts, inscriptions, and sculptures that provide valuable insights into the history and development of Buddhism in India.
 
• The **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** manages the site and has undertaken extensive conservation efforts to preserve its historical and cultural significance.
 
• Sarnath is also home to the **Archaeological Museum**, which houses a remarkable collection of artifacts, including the famous **Lion Capital of Ashoka**, which is now the national emblem of India.
